tweets.text:
Eric says the biggest mistake investors made in cloud was undersizing the market, and everyone is doing it again with AI:

"In 2014, a really common narrative was AWS is going to eat everything. There's no enterprise opportunity left.

Think about 2014 to now. You have Snowflake, direct competitor to Amazon Redshift, ran on Amazon. You're out-Amazoning Amazon on Amazon. 

Confluent and Elastic and Mongo, Databricks. Then you have the whole app layer. Datadog, $100 billion company.

The view that AWS was gonna eat everything was massively wrong because Azure and GCP were irrelevant then. 

Fast-forward to 2026, you ended up with an oligopoly. Even outside of those big three, you have Cloudflare, which is another $100 billion company.

The biggest mistake everybody made was they just undersized the market.

The market was so big that one vendor could not scale and consume it all. That whole notion right now with what you and I are seeing in AI sure feels like it rhymes.

The takeaway to me is "What if it all works?"

Be careful with labels. 

“I’m a technical trader.” 
“I’m a fundamental trader.” 
“I’m a value investor.” 
“I’m a momentum trader.” 

The moment you label yourself, you start seeing the market through that label and ignoring opportunities that don’t fit inside it.

$AMZN falls 30% to $200 and trades at one of its lowest valuations in years. The value investor says the P/E is still too high. The technical trader says it hasn’t reached his moving average. The momentum trader sees a falling stock and wants nothing to do with it.

Or take $ZIM when it was around $13. It was trading at almost half its cash value, with assets worth multiples of its market cap, yet the stock was well below its 200-day moving average. The fundamental trader sees an opportunity. The technical trader sees a chart he shouldn’t touch.

That’s the trap with labels. Your label becomes your rules, and your rules can make you blind to some of the best opportunities you will ever see.

If you ask me what kind of trader I am, I’m a logician. I’m here to make money. I don’t care if the opportunity comes from fundamentals, technicals, options, sentiment, or something else. If the logic makes sense to me and the opportunity is there, I take it.

Use every tool available to you. Don’t let a label decide what opportunities you’re allowed to see.

Risk management is mostly position sizing. Amazon falls to $200 and you think it’s a great opportunity, but you’re worried it could fall another 30%? Fine. Put 5% of your portfolio into it instead of the 20% I recommended. Even if it falls another 30%, you lost only 1.5% of your portfolio. No big deal.

Don’t put some arbitrary stop loss 5% below your entry just because you’re afraid of losing money. Stocks need room to breathe. Manage the risk by managing the size of the position, not by getting stopped out because of normal volatility.

Obviously, if the thesis that made you buy the stock completely breaks, that’s different. Then you get out because the reason you owned it no longer exists.

A Letter to My Mother & Brother (who now apparently hate me and think me a racist),

My mother is an extraordinary woman. She was born in 1943, during the height of WWII, and grew up in the back of a butcher shop on the South Side of Chicago. She married my father in 1966, and they divorced approximately 37 years later.

Since that divorce, I have coached her in stock and option trading. Her performance is exceptional, and she is up well over 40% this year.

In other words, I have helped her take 2-3 hundred grand and turn it into about $900,000 over the last few years. This includes her pulling out living expenses.

However, she and I recently had an argument.

Apparently, my younger brother follows my X account and then contacts her. He tells her that I am some kind of bitter racist and think whites are superior. She went so far as to say I don’t understand the situation because I don’t live in Chicago anymore where a lot of blacks live.

This is a joke. I live in Durham, NC, which, I believe, actually has a higher black percentage of the population than Chicago. Moreover, I live in a multi-racial household. My wife is roughly a quarter African heritage. I speak conversational Spanish. My wife, from Colombia, laughed out loud at any allegations of me being a racist.

I make comments. Such as that some women or some minority individuals get put into certain positions that white people would likely not find themselves for lack of experience. In other words, sometimes corporations or whatever promote people up the ranks to diversify.

Stating that the above sometimes occurs, does not in any way mean that I believe white men are superior.

I just want this all on the record. My little brother and mother have sometimes looked at my X posts and then accused me of racism and being a white supremist.

Nothing could be farther from the truth.

Indeed, it is my brother, whom we call Country Club Dave, and my mother who have never really lived and breathed in a true inter-racial environment.

The first man to punch me in the face was black. When I was in USMC basic training and living with many African-Americans, I became friends with some and then there were those who literally held hot irons close to my face to scare me away from an ironing board ahead of officer inspections.

I am not a racist. I am not a white supremist. I have a relationship with God.

But if I also point out hypocrisy and easy promotions on major networks, that does not equate me to a member of the KKK.

Lastly, the thing that hurt me most yesterday coming from my mother was an accusation of having no relationship with God.

As much as I love my mother, it is simply not for any human to question another human's relationship with God. Period. That is a scared relationship between each one of us and our creator. 

Romans 14:4 encapsulates it well. "Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To their own master, servants stand or fall. And they will stand, for the Lord is able to make them stand." (New International Version)

Mom, I love you. But it is not your place to question my relationship with God.

Headline: record revenue, big strategic bombshell, but EPS miss and softer margin guide.

Revenue

• vs Consensus: Better than guided
• YoY: vs -$27.6M

Backlog
• Q2 2026: $2.36B
• vs Consensus: Record
• YoY: +137%

Q3 guide:
Revenue $250M–$265M (another record)
But GAAP gross margin dropping to 29–31% (Mynaric/Motiv acquisitions weighing)
Adj. EBITDA loss widening to -$17M to -$23M

-------------------------------------------
Why the stock sold off

Three things hit sentiment:

- EPS missed (-$0.08 vs -$0.06 expected) - GAAP opex ballooned to $142M (+34% QoQ) on acquisition integration and Neutron ramp

- Gross margin guide down - Q3 GAAP gross margin guided to 29-31% vs Q2's 36%, driven by acquired lower-margin businesses

- Cash burn accelerating - Q2 FCF was -$110M; management said cash-flow positivity is 18–24 months after Neutron's first successful flight (Neutron to pad Q4 2026, so mid-2028 at earliest)

-------------------------------------------
The bigger story - this was a transformational quarter. Beck is going all-in on vertical integration:

- Acquiring Iridium (~$870M annual revenue, 66-satellite constellation, 2.5M subscribers). Creates a self-launching tier-1 space company - builds, launches, AND operates its own constellation. Closes mid-2027 pending approvals.

- Closed Mynaric (laser comms) and Motiv acquisitions
Signed $1B+ in new contracts in Q2 + post-quarter, including: $397M Space Force Flatellite contract (SB-AMTI - airborne threat tracking from space) 

- $266M Space Force HASTE contract (largest launch contract ever, 18 suborbital missions)
$160M+ in GEO satellite contracts
Neutron on track: 400+ Archimedes hot fires, Stage 1 tank production aligned with Q4 2026 pad delivery
GHOST mobile launch system announced (first pad in Kodiak, Alaska)

-------------------------------------------
Bull case

- Revenue compounding at 60%+ with visibility out years via $2.36B backlog

- Iridium changes the company structurally — moves from launch/hardware into recurring space applications revenue

- $1B+ in new contracts signed in ~3 months shows demand isn't slowing

- Neutron poised to unlock medium-lift in an environment where launch capacity is severely constrained

-------------------------------------------

Bear case / what to watch

- Cash burn is real and won't peak until Neutron flies. ~$1.2B cash gives runway but the clock is ticking

- Iridium integration risk — big acquisition, doesn't close until mid-2027, cultural/operational complexity

- Gross margin compression as lower-margin acquisitions layer in

- At $80 / $50B market cap on $234M quarterly revenue, this is priced for perfection on the 3-5 year story. Any Neutron delay or Iridium stumble hits hard

-------------------------------------------

Bottom line: Q2 was about the strategic transformation, not the quarter itself. 

The Iridium deal, $1B+ in new bookings, and Neutron progress are the real news. The stock sold off on near-term margin compression and cash burn, but the revenue trajectory and backlog growth are undeniable. The trade here is whether Neutron hits its Q4 2026 pad target and whether Iridium closes cleanly.
